report.verdict: Senior backend experience with strong payments and reliability work, though payouts ownership isn't shown.
write_up: This is a strong senior backend resume! At Tidewater, you connect Go services and production reliability work to numbers a recruiter can use. The payments work and your payq project make Cobalt Pay a sensible target.

The payment provider failover line is the model: it names your lead role, your partners and the change in failed checkouts. Your Experience section leads, but some of the most relevant Tidewater work sits below office activities. PostgreSQL and Kafka appear in Skills without examples of how you used them.

Let's bring the Go, failover and reconciliation work forward. Then add what you can about the PHP admin panel and the front-desk dashboard. For Cobalt Pay, be explicit about relevant work you've actually done in design reviews or on-call; competition for the role will matter too.

cards.line: Maintained the legacy PHP admin panel until it was retired in 2022
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see which system you maintained, but not what that involved. One example would show how you kept it useful until retirement.
cards.example: Maintained the legacy PHP admin panel until it was retired in 2022, including [maintenance work]
cards.question: What maintenance work did you do on the PHP admin panel?

cards.line: Built a jQuery dashboard for the front-desk staff
cards.cannot_tell: The users and tool are clear, but a recruiter can't tell what the dashboard showed or helped the staff do.
cards.example: Built a jQuery dashboard for the front-desk staff to [dashboard purpose]
cards.question: What did the front-desk dashboard show or help staff do?

cards.line: Migrated 60 services from EC2 to Kubernetes on EKS over nine months with no customer-facing downtime
cards.cannot_tell: For a role above senior engineer, the direction you set across teams would show how you guided a migration beyond your own work.
cards.example: Migrated 60 services from EC2 to Kubernetes on EKS over nine months with no customer-facing downtime, setting [cross-team migration direction]
cards.question: What direction, if any, did you set across teams for the migration?

cards.line: Led the payment provider failover project with the payments team, cutting failed checkouts during provider outages from 3.1% to 0.4%
cards.cannot_tell: This is one of your strongest results. Move it above the book club and office side project so a recruiter sees the payments work sooner.

fit.why: Your headline and current platform role point to senior software engineering, with backend work in Go, Kubernetes and payments.
fit.level: senior, leads a payment provider failover project and mentors interns
fit.note: Your Go rate-limiting service, payq library and finance reconciliation work are relevant to Cobalt Pay. Bring those closer to the top, and use concrete examples wherever you can substantiate the posting's requirements.
